sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the west side of the Ridgefield Park business and residential district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Summit runs along the top and Mt. Vernon along the bottom; Paulson Avenue and Depot Avenue cross the sheet from top to bottom, with Lincoln Avenue on the right edge and Webster, Park and Grove crossing between them. The blocks between Paulson and Lincoln are residential, with frame dwellings, many of two stories, on narrow lots with small sheds and garages. The Reinhart Hotel, with a bowling alley and hall, stands on Park near Paulson Avenue, and a large garage with a capacity of forty cars, a show room and a concrete-floored section occupies the corner of Grove and Paulson Avenue. Depot Avenue is lined with dwellings and, further down, the City Storage warehouse, a sash and door mill with power and electric light, and other sheds. A diagonal band of railroad right of way runs from the upper left to the lower centre beside Railroad Avenue, carrying the West Shore R.R. and the N.Y.S. & W. R.R. with many yard tracks, a cement warehouse and a coal shed. The Bergen Building Block Co., a cement block works with an office, power plant and iron structure shown from plans, stands at the lower left. Water pipes of six inches are drawn along most streets. The upper left corner is mostly blank, and the margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 7, 8, 3 and 4.
notes: Summit, Webster, Park, Grove and Mt. Vernon are Summit Street, Webster Street, Park Street, Grove Street and Mount Vernon Street today.
Paulson Avenue is Paulison Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The printed Mt. is written out as Mount in the street list.
scale 50 ft; configured by a helper

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the commercial centre of Ridgefield Park along Main, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The part runs from Summit and Poplar at the top to Mt. Vernon at the bottom, and from Lincoln Avenue on the left to Bergen Avenue on the right, with Webster, Park and Grove crossing between them. Main is lined with brick stores, a printing office, a plumbing shop, a hardware warehouse, sheds and auto stalls, and two banks stand at its corners with Mt. Vernon. Public and social buildings include the City Hall and a drug store on Main at Park, the Knights of Columbus hall on Park at Bergen Avenue, the Park Street Meeting House on Park, and Christ Lutheran Church near Bergen Avenue at Mt. Vernon. The blocks west of Main and east of the commercial frontage are residential, with frame dwellings, some of them two and a half stories, on narrow lots, a few concrete-block garages and many private automobile sheds. Water pipes of six and eight inches are drawn along the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Blank areas along the top and bottom edges belong to sheets 8, 4 and 5, and the margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 2 and 10. Watts Court and Spruce Avenue appear only as stubs below Mt. Vernon at the bottom edge, beside the printed scale of feet.
notes: Spruce Av. is Spruce Street in OpenStreetMap; its junction with Mt. Vernon at the bottom edge is drawn narrow and was excluded from control.
Summit, Poplar, Webster, Park, Grove, Mt. Vernon and Main are Summit Street, Poplar Street, Webster Street, Park Street, Grove Street, Mount Vernon Street and Main Street today.
City Hall stands on Main at Park; K. of C. Hall on Park at Bergen Avenue.
50 ft. Centre of the village along Main between Summit/Poplar and Mt. Vernon, Lincoln Av to Bergen Av; City Hall, K. of C. Hall. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the south-western part of the Ridgefield Park centre between Mt. Vernon at the top and Christie at the bottom, and between the Hackensack River on the left and Main on the right edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. A broad band of railroad right of way, with the N.Y.S. & W. R.R. and the W.S. R.R. and many tracks, curves down the left of the sheet; the passenger station, a waiting room, a freight house, a second passenger station and the Park Lumber & Supply Co. lumber shed lie beside it. Between Herbert and Spruce Avenue are blocks 85, 86 and 87, subdivided into narrow vacant lots, with a post office and a one-storey tile building on Watts Ct. Along Main on the right the sheet is built up with brick and concrete commercial buildings: garages with capacities of 30, 45 and 20 cars, drug stores, a show room, the Rialto Motion Pictures theatre and rows of small stores. South of Cedar the blocks 95, 96, 97, 98 and 99 are mainly frame dwellings of two stories with small sheds, with a large dwelling standing alone in block 96. The lower left of the sheet is the Hackensack River, shown as tide water with the lettering Borough of Little Ferry on the far shore, and a compass rose stands in the open water. Pipes of six inches are drawn along Mt. Vernon, Cedar, Pine, Hobart and Christie, and the margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 2, 3, 5 and 11.
notes: Mt. Vernon, Herbert, Cedar, Pine, Hobart, Christie and Main are Mount Vernon Street, Herbert Street, Cedar Street, Pine Street, Hobart Street, Christie Street and Main Street today.
Spruce Av. is Spruce Street in OpenStreetMap; Watts Ct. is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The printed Mt. is written out as Mount in the street list.
Main is drawn only on its west side on this sheet; its junctions on the right edge were measured from one drawn edge.
scale 50 ft; configured by a helper

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the centre of Ridgefield Park south of Mt. Vernon, between Main on the left and Euclid Avenue on the right, and from Mt. Vernon at the top to Christie at the bottom. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bergen Avenue crosses the middle and Cedar and Hobart divide the sheet into rows of blocks. The upper left block, along Main, holds the commercial frontage: brick stores, a bakery with ovens, the Fire Department Hose Co. No. 1 with a fire bell on an iron tower, a garage and the First M.E. Church with steam heat and electric light. Block 90, north of Cedar on the right, has the Bishop Manor Club House and frame dwellings along Euclid Avenue. Between Cedar and Hobart stand the two public institutions of the district, Washington High School with its auditorium and Public School No. 1 with a second auditorium, both of brick and drawn in pink, with hydrant and hose connections marked. The rest of that row is dwellings, a lumber shed, a Masonic Hall and a few small shops. The bottom row between Hobart and Christie is lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few sheds and a tile and asbestos shingle building. Water pipes of six and eight inches run in the streets. Pine appears only as a stub at the left edge, and the margins carry the numbers of sheets 3, 4, 10 and 11.
notes: Mt. Vernon, Cedar, Hobart, Christie and Main are Mount Vernon Street, Cedar Street, Hobart Street, Christie Street and Main Street today.
The printed Mt. is written out as Mount in the street list.
Christie meets Main at two OpenStreetMap nodes about 26 m apart (Christie jogs); both were excluded from control.
scale 50 ft; configured by a helper

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the southern edge of the Ridgefield Park centre where the village meets the Hackensack River, the railroad and Overpeck Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. A wide band of railroad right of way, carrying the N.Y.S. & W. R.R. and the W.S. R.R. with many yard tracks, runs diagonally from the top centre to the lower right. West of the tracks lies the Flintkote Co. Inc. Plant No. 2, a large felt and shingle works of brick and steel with a beater room, mill, pump house, rag receiving room and warehouse, a gray No. 2 Mill building by the river, and a note on its watchman, clock, power, steam, sprinklers and fire pump. Below it are the yards of Brewster & Son, building material and coal, with long lumber sheds, coal pockets, a cement warehouse, a ware house and a scattered lumber pile, reached from Bergen Turnpike, which crosses the lower part of the sheet with a bridge to Little Ferry on its west end. A freight house and the Little Ferry depot stand by the tracks, and a sash and door warehouse and greenhouses lie south of the turnpike beside Overpeck Creek. East of the tracks, Main, Ridgefield Avenue and Union bound residential blocks of frame dwellings, with brick stores, the Park Moving Picture Theatre, a roofing warehouse and the Imperial Brush Co. and Victory Dress Co. building at the Union and Bergen Turnpike corner. Winant Avenue crosses the top edge, and the margins carry the numbers of sheets 3, 4, 5 and 6.
notes: Winant Avenue is drawn narrower than today's street and was left out of control.
College Pl. is College Place and Ridgefield Av. is Ridgefield Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Orchard and Union are Orchard Street and Union Street, and Main is Main Street.
The bridge to Little Ferry is marked on Bergen Turnpike at the west edge, with a 20 inch water pipe.
The compass rose points north about 27 degrees to the left of the page, matching the fitted rotation.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the north-western part of Ridgefield Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. North Avenue runs along the top edge, where a lettered line marks the village limits and the Borough of Bogota beyond. Central Avenue and Hackensack Avenue cross the sheet, and numbered streets run down it: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th above Hackensack Avenue, and S. 3rd, S. 4th and S. 5th below it, ending at Summit near the bottom right edge. Paulison Avenue and Depot Avenue meet Summit at the lower right. Most of the sheet is residential, with frame dwellings of one and two stories on narrow lots, many with small sheds and garages, laid out in numbered blocks 1 to 11 and 43 to 46. Swedish Luther Church stands near 4th and 5th between Central and Hackensack. On the left a wide band of railroad right of way with the N.Y.S. & W. R.R. and W.S. R.R. tracks runs diagonally beside Railroad Avenue, and beyond it lie two works on the bank of the Hackensack River: the Adiel Vandeweghe furrier plant, with a hair vault, dye house and drying rooms, and the Bogota Folding Box Co. and Box Mfg. plant, drawn in pink with a note on its watchman, clock, power, steam and fire pumps. The river fills the lower left, with the City of Hackensack on the far shore. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 2 and 8.
notes: The numbered streets are 1st Street to 6th Street in OpenStreetMap; the S. 3rd, S. 4th and S. 5th Street names south of Hackensack Avenue are 3rd Street, 4th Street and 5th Street there.
North Avenue, Central Avenue, Hackensack Avenue, Railroad Avenue and Paulison Avenue are the same in OpenStreetMap; Summit is Summit Street.
Rustin Street is a short street near Paulison Avenue, read as printed at small size; it is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
A line at the top reads Borough of Bogota Beyond Village Limits.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the northern residential half of the Ridgefield Park village, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. North Avenue and Arthur run along the top, where the sheet adjoins the Borough of Bogota and the Teaneck Township village limits, and Summit and Poplar run along the bottom. Main crosses the sheet from top to bottom, with 6th, 7th and 8th to its west and Hanson, Cutter and Bergen Avenue to its east, and Central Avenue, Hackensack Avenue, Grand Avenue and Union Pl. cross the sheet from side to side. The sheet is almost entirely frame dwellings of one and two stories on narrow lots, laid out in numbered blocks 13 to 75, with small sheds and garages and few commercial buildings. The public and institutional buildings are the Neighborhood Reformed Church at the top, the Lincoln Public School No. 4 with the Fire Dept. house beside it on Hackensack Avenue, the First Church of Christ Scientist on the diagonal part of Hackensack Avenue, and a tract occupied by the American Legion at 7th. A small works, Columbia Machine Wks., stands at Paulison Avenue and Preston, and a shingle works lies at the foot of 6th. Hackensack Avenue runs diagonally through blocks 48 and 49 and a short Lane joins it. Six-inch water pipes are drawn along the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 7, 9, 2, 3 and 10.
notes: Arthur, Edwin, Gordon, Hazelton, Austin, Preston, Summit, Poplar, Main and Cutter are Arthur Street, Edwin Street, Gordon Street, Hazelton Street, Austin Street, Preston Street, Summit Street, Poplar Street, Main Street and Cutter Street today; Highland Pl. and Union Pl. are Highland Place and Union Place.
Hanson is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
A printed line at the top reads Village Limits; the top margin also reads Teaneck Township Village Limits at the right.
Cutter Street is drawn about 33 feet wide against 50 feet in the parcels, so its junctions were measured with narrow pairs.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the eastern edge of the built-up part of Ridgefield Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Arthur runs along the top left and Poplar along the bottom, Cutter forms the left edge, and Teaneck Rd. runs from top to bottom through the right half with Overpeck Avenue to its east. The left half is closely built residential blocks, 18 to 72, of frame dwellings of one and two stories on narrow lots, with Edwin, Gordon, Hazelton, Highland Pl., Grand Av., Union Pl. and Preston crossing Roosevelt Av., which carries a second name, Gibson, in parentheses, and Carrolton, Pershing, Euclid Avenue and Hudson Avenue joining them. Roosevelt Public School, a brick building with steam heat and electric light, stands in block 28, a fire department hook and ladder house on Roosevelt Av. at Hazelton, and St. Mark's Episcopal Church with its parish house on Preston at Euclid Avenue. The Home for Aged People stands at the top beside Teaneck Rd. East of Teaneck Rd. the sheet is mostly open land in large lots and unbuilt tracts, with scattered houses, a few dwellings along East Grand Av. in block 148, and a short row of houses on Preston and Overpeck Avenue in blocks 69, 70 and 146. Large unlettered areas on the right carry the references S-11 and S-12 for the adjoining sheets, and the margins carry the numbers of sheets 8 and 10.
notes: Arthur, Edwin, Gordon, Hazelton, Preston, Poplar and Cutter are Arthur Street, Edwin Street, Gordon Street, Hazelton Street, Preston Street, Poplar Street and Cutter Street today.
Roosevelt Av. is drawn about 33 feet wide against 50 feet in the parcels, and its junctions were left out of control.

The printed Gibson and Carrolton, each in parentheses, are alternative names for the streets lettered Roosevelt Av. and the street between blocks 67 and 68A; Gibson and Carrolton are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Teaneck Township appears in the top left corner with Village Limits.

sheet-10-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 10 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north slightly to the upper left, and covers the residential district east of the centre of Ridgefield Park. Bergen Avenue runs along the left edge, followed to the east by Euclid Avenue, Hudson Avenue, Teaneck Road and Overpeck Avenue, with Overlook Avenue along part of the right edge; Poplar, Park, Mt. Vernon, Cedar, Hobart and Christie cross them from top to bottom, and a short unnamed street runs east from Overpeck Avenue to the right edge. The blocks are almost entirely frame dwellings with private garages, set on regular lots, with a few brick or tile houses and a short row of brick stores on Teaneck Road at Cedar. Several churches are drawn: the First Presbyterian Church on Poplar, the Union Church on Park, St. Francis Church with its class rooms on Bergen Avenue, the First Congregational Church on Euclid Avenue at Cedar and the First Baptist Church on Euclid Avenue at Hobart, and the Ridgefield Park Hebrew Association stands on Bergen Avenue. An aluminum box making shop occupies a small building on Hobart east of Overpeck Avenue. The block at the lower right is laid out but sparsely built. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are drawn along the streets. The left margin overlaps sheet 5, whose number is printed in the blank area, and the lower left corner of the sheet is given to a small inset, part 2.
notes: Overlook is printed as "Overlook (Av.)", with the suffix in parentheses.
The street printed "Not Named" east of Overpeck Avenue is Morningside Lane in OpenStreetMap.
Poplar and Hobart jog where they cross Teaneck Road and Overpeck Avenue respectively; the modern junctions carry residuals of 2 to 3 m there.

100 ft. sheet-10-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 10 is a small inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, framed by a heavy line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It continues the sheet beyond its right edge, where the number 10 is printed on the unnamed 30 foot street running east from Overpeck Avenue; the same number marks that street in the inset. The inset shows the end of that street at a 50 foot street, also lettered Not Named, which runs up the inset to the edge of the surveyed area, and block 110 to the east of it with the small frame clubhouse of The Pines Tennis Club. A few lots with one small building lie on the west side of the 50 foot street. The rest of the inset is blank. The part has no junction between two named streets; it is placed by points carried from part 1 through the boxed number 10 on the unnamed 30 foot street, assuming the inset keeps part 1's scale and orientation. The two unnamed streets correspond to Morningside Lane and Overlook Avenue today.
notes: Both streets are printed "Not Named"; they correspond to Morningside Lane (30 ft) and Overlook Avenue (50 ft) in OpenStreetMap.
Placed by three points carried from sheet-10-1 through the boxed 10; low confidence in rotation.

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, and covers the southern residential district of Ridgefield Park between Christie at the top and South and the Bergen Turnpike at the bottom. Main runs down the left side, and Ridgefield Avenue, Euclid Avenue, Garden, Laurel, Voorhees Place, Queen Esthers Court and Teaneck Road cross the part from top to bottom, with Hille Place and Hanson Place east of Teaneck Road; Brinkerhoff, Brewster Avenue, Emerson, Winant Avenue and East Winant Avenue, Orchard, College Place and Henry run across it, and Union, Edison, Laurel and Orchard reach South, Chestnut and the Bergen Turnpike in the lower blocks. Truitt runs off to the right below Teaneck Road. The district is almost entirely frame dwellings with private garages on regular lots, with a few concrete-block and tile buildings and a small group of stores near Main. Institutions include the Grant Public School No. 3 on Henry at Teaneck Road, the Ridgefield Park fire department Hose Co. No. 2 and Hook and Ladder Co. No. 1 on Euclid Avenue, Hose Co. No. 4 on Teaneck Road, and the Junior Order Club House on Ridgefield Avenue. Blocks 133 and 134 on the right are laid out but largely unbuilt. The lower left corner of the sheet is taken by an inset, part 2, framed by a heavy line, and the margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 4, 5, 6, 10 and 12.
notes: Emerson is printed "Emerson (Division)"; the index says "Division, see Emerson". It is Emerson Street today.
Winant Avenue is drawn about 42 ft wide against a 75 ft right-of-way today; its junctions were left out of control (residuals of 3 to 4 m, widened since).
The drawn junction of Brinkerhoff and Main lies about 9 m from the modern one (Main Street Bypass); it was excluded.
Teaneck Rd. at Voorhees Pl. disagreed with the fit by 12 m and was excluded.

100 ft. Winant Avenue left out of control (drawn 42 ft, today 75 ft, junctions 3 to 4 m off).

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is an inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, framed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, but turned so that Main runs straight up the page rather than at the slant it has on the main map. It shows the west side of Main from Christie southward, next to the West Shore Railroad, whose right of way runs down the left edge. Homestead Place runs from Christie to Brinkerhoff between blocks 105 and 104, and Christie and Brinkerhoff cross from the railroad to Main, where short labels mark Christie Street, Brinkerhoff Street, Brewster Avenue and Winant Avenue leaving to the east. The blocks hold frame dwellings and a stone dwelling on Homestead Place, and block 106 below Brinkerhoff is sparsely built with a few dwellings. A north arrow and the scale note are printed in the inset, with the numbers of the adjoining sheets 4, 6 and 11 and the marker S-4. Christie jogs about 100 feet where it meets Main, so its two sides are drawn on different lines.
notes: The railroad along the left edge is lettered W.S.R.R. (West Shore Railroad).
Placed on three points (two hand-picked); the modern Brinkerhoff Street / Main Street junction is about 27 m from the drawn one and was excluded.
The inset is drawn about 17 degrees from the main map's orientation.

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 12 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north slightly to the upper left, and covers the southern tip of Ridgefield Park where the Bergen Turnpike runs southeast along the bank of Overpeck Creek toward the bridge to Ridgefield. Above the turnpike lie residential blocks on South, Chestnut and Elm between Edison and Orchard, and Oak, Maple and Teaneck Road run down from Elm to the turnpike, with Birch east of Teaneck Road. The blocks hold frame dwellings and private garages on narrow lots, with large unbuilt blocks 134 and 140 on the right. Between the turnpike and the creek are Overpeck Park with a dance hall, the Bergen Pike Hygeia Ice Co. plant on Eucker, the Overpeck Boat Club on the creek bank, a large garage for 90 cars with a show room, the paper box factory of Thomas S. Taranto, the Horton Sweet Co. candy works, a job printing shop and two service stations with gasoline tanks. Overpeck Creek, lettered as tide water, fills the lower left of the part, with the Borough of Ridgefield on the far bank. The turnpike leaves the sheet at the right edge over a branch of the creek, marked 12 where it continues in the inset in the lower left corner (part 2). Lots along the turnpike carry the house numbers 801 to 916.
notes: The drawn Eucker and the Chestnut / Teaneck Rd. junction lie 8 and 14 m from the modern junctions and were excluded.
Overpeck Creek is lettered "(Tide Water)"; the far bank is lettered "Boro. of Ridgefield".

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (South to Bergen Turnpike, Edison to Teaneck Rd and Birch; Overpeck Creek); part 2 inset lower left: Bergen Turnpike lots 901-911 east of the creek branch, placed by points carried from part 1 through the boxed 12.

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12 is an inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, framed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It continues the Bergen Turnpike east of the right edge of the main map, beyond the narrow branch of Overpeck Creek where both parts print the number 12 in a box. The turnpike runs across the inset with lots numbered 901 to 911 on its south side, between the road and the creek bank, in the area marked S-7; they hold a few frame dwellings, private garages and gasoline tanks. North of the road the lots of block 140 are laid out but not built on. Overpeck Creek, lettered as tide water, fills the lower part of the inset, with the Borough of Ridgefield on its far bank in the main map beside it. A north arrow and the scale note are printed in the inset. The part has no street junction; it is placed by carrying three points from the main map through the matching box at the creek crossing, assuming the inset keeps the main map's scale and orientation, which its road and box agree with.
notes: Placed by points carried from sheet-12-1 through the boxed number 12 at the creek crossing; low confidence along the road.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (South to Bergen Turnpike, Edison to Teaneck Rd and Birch; Overpeck Creek); part 2 inset lower left: Bergen Turnpike lots 901-911 east of the creek branch, placed by points carried from part 1 through the boxed 12.
